structured_output.what_is_happening: A 3-day-old pump.fun token (migrated to PumpSwap about 3.2 days ago), named after a real open-source GitHub repo of AI-agent SKILL.md playbooks (sickn33/agentic-awesome-skills), came back to life suddenly. Almost all of its 24h volume (~$21.8k of $32.8k) came in the last hour, and price is up ~400% in that hour to a ~$35k market cap, still below its ATH of ~$52k. Flow is buy-heavy (139 buys / 71 sells in h1; 96 unique buyers vs 52 sellers). But the last 15 minutes are flat (+3.7%) after +46% over 30 minutes, so the burst is cooling. The GeckoTerminal Twitter handle 'sickn33' matches the GitHub owner. That hints the trigger could be the repo author noticing, endorsing or claiming the token. Paid alerts or bots are also possible. Nothing in the packet confirms either.

narrative.description: The token wraps a real, popular-looking GitHub repo for AI coding-agent skills (Claude/Codex SKILL.md). It sits in the 'tokenize a real dev/GitHub project' and AI-agent tooling meta. That story beats a pure meme, and a real developer tie-in makes a revival possible.
narrative.why_spreading: The volume spike on a dormant coin that is 3+ days old points to an outside catalyst. The likeliest one is the repo author (sickn33) engaging, or the token being shared in dev/AI-agent circles. That can't be checked without X data. Two copycat AAS tokens (0 liquidity) were created in the last few hours, so some people are watching the name.

token_connection.why_this_token: It is the oldest live AAS/'Agentic Awesome Skills' token with real liquidity. It links the GitHub repo directly, and its GeckoTerminal handle matches the repo owner.
token_connection.competing_tokens: Three same-ticker tokens: 2nQF... (created ~1.6h before this one, $0.81 liquidity), and HfY3... and DuoY... (both created in the last ~day, 0 liquidity, ~$3k mcap). None has meaningful liquidity.

authenticity.evidence: Buyer breadth is decent (96 unique h1 buyers), there is no paid DexScreener boost or ad, dev holds 0.8%, and the top10 excluding the AMM is 23%. On the other side, GMGN tags 253 bundler and 372 fresh wallets among traders and bot/degen share is 41%, so a lot of the flow is automated or farmed. GMGN page visits are very low (8), which means little broad retail attention so far.
authenticity.uncertainty: The cause of the revival can't be seen. It could be a real repo-author endorsement or a coordinated bundle pump into a thin pool.

structural_risks: Liquidity is thin (~$15k), so a few wallets selling can knock price down 50% fast
Wallet data is bundler- and fresh-heavy (253 bundlers, 372 fresh), which fits manufactured volume
Momentum has already stalled in the last 15 minutes, before the 25-minute-delayed entry
Previous ATH ~$52k mcap gives overhead supply from earlier holders who are now back near breakeven
LP is burned at 100%, so a literal liquidity pull is unlikely. The death risk is a dump and a fade

structured_output.counterargument: The token ties to a real, relevant developer project, and the matching 'sickn33' handle suggests the repo owner may be involved. In 2026, an endorsement from a real GitHub developer can move a $35k coin to $100k+ within hours. Buy-heavy flow with broad unique buyers and no paid promotion is what an early organic run looks like, and $70k (a 2x) is only slightly above the old ATH.
unknowns: Whether the repo author actually tweeted or endorsed the token
What triggered the h1 volume spike
Whether the bundler wallets are the ones now holding the supply
Price action between detection and entry 25 minutes later

structured_output.thesis: This is a dormant real-dev/AI-agent token that revived with 5x in one hour. The story is better than average and there is a plausible tie to the dev. But the coin has already made its move, momentum is stalling, and the pool is thin and bundle-heavy. After a 25-minute delay, a 2x (to ~$70k+, above the prior ATH) is harder to get than a 50% retrace. I expect a fade unless the repo owner confirms involvement.
